page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v6 is an entry-level compute-oriented virtual machine within Azure's general-purpose series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573B processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Hardware allocation consists of 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and access to a 260 MB shared L3 cache. Advanced CPU instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 4.0 GB, establishing a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle any local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote storage, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable. There are no hardware accelerators or GPUs present, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data demonstrates robust single-threaded compute capacity driven by the 4.2 GHz clock speed and modern architecture. In single-core assessments, the instance achieved a Geekbench score of 2134.0 (top 25%) and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.36 GB/sec (top 25%). However, overall multi-core and memory throughput reflect the constraints of a single physical core and a small memory footprint. Multi-core performance placed low, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2620.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 1984.78. Memory bandwidth tests indicated 20.87 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 14.17 GB/sec for uncached write blocks, each falling into the lower quartile of cloud instances.

The qualitative profile of the D2ls_v6 represents a cost-effective alternative for workloads that need dedicated high clock speed compute cycles but do not require large memory arrays or high multi-threaded scaling. Suitable application domains include lightweight single-threaded microservices, basic build agents, task queue workers, and small-scale web service frontends where 4 GB of RAM is sufficient.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v6 is a virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8573B processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a lean memory profile of 4.0 GB RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), the instance provides no bundled local disk storage and zero GPUs, relying on Premium Storage remote disks. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic extensions. Performance profiles show strong single-threaded CPU execution, scoring in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core and gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall in the lower quartiles due to the two-thread limit and smaller memory channel capacity. This instance serves well for low-overhead compute tasks, lightweight utility services, single-threaded processing, and basic development workloads that do not demand expansive system memory.
